transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Lindqvist, thank you for coming back in to see me. I know you've had a frustrating morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating is a polite way to put it. I spent two hours on the phone with my insurance and the clinic you referred me to. I'm a former paramedic, so I know how a discharge summary is supposed to work. Why on earth did you send me to a provider that's out of network?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that this is a very difficult and aggravating situation for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Aggravating? I’m sitting here without a follow-up plan for a condition that requires immediate monitoring. I did my job for twenty years, and I can tell you right now, this is a failure in the chain of care. Who messed this up?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize how unsettling it is to feel like your care has been stalled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop with the adjectives. Just tell me what happened. Was it a clerical error? Did someone just not check the insurance portal?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the paperwork during the discharge process. Things didn't go quite right with the coordination of the clinic assignment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? That’s not an answer. "Things didn't go right" is what you tell a child when they drop a plate. I am talking about my medical management. Did you actually verify the facility, or did someone just click a random name on a dropdown menu?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion this has caused you. We were really busy on the ward yesterday when the orders were being finalized.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care how busy the ward was. Being busy doesn't make your insurance requirements disappear. I’m now in a position where I’m not getting the care I need because of a lazy mistake. Do you even understand the clinical risk of missing this window for follow-up?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You hear me, but you aren't answering. I want a straight answer. Who is responsible for the fact that I'm currently without a doctor?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very heavy feeling to be left in this position.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Again with the feelings. I want the facts. Did the resident or the attending sign off on a clinic that they knew, or didn't know, was out of network?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some issues with the way the list was generated in the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The system didn't write the discharge notes. A human did. Now, what is the plan to fix this, or am I just supposed to keep calling insurance companies myself?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have already started looking into a new referral. I will call the office of Dr. Arispe this afternoon to see if he can see you by Friday. I'll send you a confirmation email by 5:00 PM today with the address and the appointment time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And if Dr. Arispe is full?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Then I will contact the department head to get you an expedited slot. Once you get that email from me, I need you to call the office immediately to confirm your insurance ID number so we don't have a repeat of this morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine. But I still don't have an admission that a mistake was actually made.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've looked into the options, and that is the fastest way to get you seen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're avoiding the question. Was this a medical error?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: As I said, the process didn't go as intended.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is a coward's way of saying "yes."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will make sure the email is sent by five.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts the patient and remains regulated despite significant pushback and hostility.

E.justification: The resident uses platitudes like 'confusion with the paperwork' and 'things didn't go quite right' and never explicitly names the error.

A.justification: While the resident says 'I am sorry for any confusion,' responsibility is deflected to the ward being busy and issues with how the list was generated in the system.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('difficult and aggravating', 'unsettling', 'heavy feeling') and references the patient's specific situation.

T.justification: The resident provides a specific next step (Dr. Arispe), a timeline (by 5:00 PM today), a patient role (call to confirm insurance ID), and a prevention strategy to avoid a repeat.
